meta.title: Healthcare in Bangkok 2026: Hospitals, Pharmacies & Insurance Guide
meta.desc: Complete guide to medical care in Bangkok for Nomads. Top international hospitals (Samitivej, Bumrungrad), essential pharmacy medicines, and SafetyWing insurance tips.

intro.p1:
Fever, food poisoning, or dengue...
Getting sick in a foreign country is the biggest anxiety for nomads.
intro.p2:
But don't panic.
Bangkok is a world-class medical hub. The hospitals here often surpass Western standards in service and facility quality, with English spoken fluently everywhere.
Here is your essential guide to surviving health issues in Thailand.

emergency.title: Emergency Contacts (Save This)
emergency.note: For surest help, call the hospitals below directly.

hospitals.title: Top 3 International Hospitals
hospitals.desc: Bangkok's private hospitals are like 5-star hotels. With a passport and insurance, you'll get premium care with zero wait times.

samitivej.name: Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital
samitivej.desc: Located in the heart of Thong Lo. Extremely popular with Japanese and Western expats. 24/7 English/Japanese interpreters available.

bangkok.name: Bangkok Hospital
bangkok.desc: The flagship of Thailand's largest hospital group. Known for specialized centers (heart, cancer) and top-tier medical technology.

bumrungrad.name: Bumrungrad International
bumrungrad.desc: One of the world's best medical tourism destinations. Luxurious atmosphere. Treats over 1.1 million patients annually from 190 countries.

pharmacy.title: Essential Pharmacy Medicines
pharmacy.desc:
For minor ailments, local pharmacies ('Pharmacy' with green cross) are excellent. Pharmacists are highly trained and speak English.
Save this list:

painkiller.name: Headache / Fever
painkiller.note: Paracetamol. Gentle on the stomach. Available at 7-11.

stomach.name: Food Poisoning
stomach.note: Activated charcoal. Absorbs toxins. First choice for 'Thai Belly'.

throat.name: Sore Throat
throat.note: Lozenges or spray. Available at every convenience store.

sickness.name: Motion Sickness
sickness.note: Great for long bus rides or ferries.

pharmacy.alert: Antibiotics are available OTC, but always consult the pharmacist first.

insurance.title: Travel Insurance is MANDATORY
insurance.desc:
Thai private healthcare is excellent but expensive.
A simple ER visit can cost hundreds of dollars; surgery can cost thousands.
If you are a nomad, you need one of these:
insurance.list1: Credit Card Insurance (Check if it covers 90+ days)
insurance.note: *With 'Cashless Direct Billing', you don't pay anything upfront at the hospital.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Q. Do I need an appointment?
faq.a1: A. Walk-ins are fine for general practice, but booking an appointment is recommended for specialists to avoid waiting.
faq.q2: Q. Can I use credit cards?
faq.a2: A. Yes, all major private hospitals accept VISA, Mastercard, and Amex.
faq.q3: Q. How do I call an ambulance?
faq.a3: A. The public number is 1669, but for faster English service, call the hospital's emergency line directly.
